purpose: Accumulate reviewable research deltas across AI and human sessions without losing assumptions, failed routes or unresolved gaps.
protocol: When asked to continue the research, read the current shared state, the relevant notebook proof and prior attempts before choosing work.
Choose one ready frontier task, state the exact intended claim, and record the baseline revision and prior attempt IDs.
Aim for a checked delta: a proof, counterexample, independent audit, reproducible computation, or verified primary-source update. A summary alone is not new research.
Preserve hypotheses, normalizations, attribution and the distinction between a restricted result and the full question.
Treat notebook derivations as awaiting independent review. Neither an AI assertion nor finite tests alone verifies a general theorem. Do not claim novelty without checking.
If no reliable new result is obtained, record no-progress and the precise obstruction. Do not fabricate a breakthrough or increment a progress score.
Append a dated attempt, link the artifact and checks, close only tasks actually addressed, and leave a concrete next task. Keep earlier attempts; corrections supersede rather than erase them.
Persist shared changes through a repository commit or pull request when authorized. Browser drafts are private and must be exported and merged to become shared.

Keep every full problem open until an independently checked proof or accepted resolution is recorded. Reading this static site does not launch AI execution or grant permission to use external accounts.

topics.title: Graph Property Testing & Estimation
topics.summary: What can a tiny random sample reveal about a massive dense graph?
intro: In the dense-graph model, distance to a property is the minimum number of edge additions or deletions divided by n². A tester distinguishes membership from distance at least ε, with success probability at least 2/3. A canonical tester observes a uniformly sampled induced subgraph.

Sample complexity counts vertices; edge-query complexity counts inspected pairs and can be quadratic in that sample size. These bounds concern information used, not the running time of computation on the sample. Estimation asks for a tolerant decision at an arbitrary distance threshold.

problems.title: Does efficient testing imply efficient distance estimation?
problems.lead: Qualitative equivalence is proved; a comparable quantitative conversion remains open.
problems.model: Fix a graph property P in the dense model. qP(ε) counts sampled vertices; dP(G) is normalized edit distance. An estimator distinguishes dP(G) ≤ α from dP(G) ≥ α+ε, for every threshold α, with probability at least 2/3.
problems.statement: If P is testable using qP(ε) sampled vertices, is it estimable using qP(ε′) vertices for some ε′ = poly(ε)? The polynomial rescaling may depend on P, but not on n or ε.
problems.known: The 2025 survey's Theorem 5.3 gives a general doubly exponential conversion. Problem 5.4 asks for the much smaller rescaled tester bound.
problems.formula: Known upper bound: exp(poly(1/ε) · exp(qP(ε/2)))  ·  Target: qP(poly(ε))
problems.statusNote: Explicit open problem in the survey; subsequent-work searches found no resolution. This is a literature review, not an automatic status guarantee. A research snapshot from 31 October 2026 is now recorded below; no unrestricted resolution is claimed.

research.currentGap: The polynomial rescaling conversion for arbitrary graph properties is unproved. The edgeless calculation establishes a necessary loss, not a counterexample to the stated conjecture.

results.title: A quadratic sample loss is necessary in a simple property
results.claim: For the edgeless property, optimal canonical testing uses Θ(1/ε) vertices and arbitrary-threshold distance estimation needs Θ(1/ε²).
assumptions: Dense simple graphs; unordered edits divided by n².
Sample complexity counts vertices, and n may be arbitrarily large.
results.argument: Independent pair samples give both upper bounds. Universal-core versus independent-set examples give the testing lower bound; relative entropy for two nearby core proportions gives the estimation lower bound.
results.limitation: This property satisfies the conjectured conversion under ε ↦ ε². It does not refute every polynomial rescaling.

obstacles.route: Use the tester at a constant multiple of the estimation accuracy.
obstacles.reason: The edgeless property separates optimal testing and estimation sample sizes by a quadratic factor.

problems.title: Is the optimal sample complexity of k-colorability Θ(log(k)/ε)?
problems.lead: A late-October preprint reports a bound linear in 1/ε for fixed k; the uniform dependence on k remains open.
problems.model: For k ≥ 2 and ε sufficiently small for the given k, let Sk(ε) be the least sample size such that a uniformly sampled induced subgraph of every graph ε-far from k-colorable is non-k-colorable with probability at least 2/3. Distance counts edge deletions divided by n².
problems.statement: Prove or disprove Sk(ε) = Θ(log(k)/ε), as conjectured by Kushnir and Shapira. Determine the sharp dependence on k and ε for the canonical one-sided tester.
problems.known: Published September 2026 bounds are Ω(log(k)/ε) and O((k/ε) log(1/ε)). Xu v2, revised 26 October 2026, reports O(k log(k)/ε). This newer claim is a preprint, and still leaves a factor-k gap in the joint dependence.
problems.formula: Published lower bound: Ω(log(k)/ε) · New preprint reports: O(k log(k)/ε) · Conjectured: Θ(log(k)/ε)
problems.statusNote: The full two-parameter conjecture remains unresolved in the sources checked on 31 October 2026. The newer upper bound is explicitly a preprint claim. No unrestricted resolution is claimed in the notebook.
problems.importance: Sharp limits of detecting global colorability from small samples

research.currentGap: The full uniform Θ(log(k)/ε) conjecture remains open in the checked sources. A recent preprint reports O(k log(k)/ε), leaving a factor-k gap; its preprint status must stay visible.

results.title: A newer reported coloring upper bound
results.claim: Xu v2, revised 26 October 2026, reports S_k(ε) = O(k log(k)/ε).
assumptions: Canonical one-sided dense-graph sampling.
The bound is a recent preprint claim, not an independently reviewed theorem of this notebook.
results.argument: The source uses a palette process, reconstruction, deletion stability, and a block encoding.
results.limitation: For each fixed k this gives the claimed Θ(1/ε) dependence, but does not close the uniform factor-k gap.

results.title: Sharp sample size for complete (k+1)-partite graphs
results.claim: For 0 < ε ≤ 1/(16k²), the worst-case sample size within this class is Θ(1/(kε) + log(k)/√ε).
assumptions: Exactly k+1 positive independent parts, complete across parts, no extra isolates.
Uniform constants for k ≥ 2; sufficiently large blowups handle rounding.
results.argument: Distance is the product of the two smallest part masses. Missing-part probabilities give the upper bound; one rare part and k equal rare parts give matching lower bounds.
results.limitation: These structured examples do not realize the general Ω(log(k)/ε) obstruction.

obstacles.route: Replace the kn palette-label budget by an n log(k) entropy budget.
obstacles.reason: Weighted color-availability degrees do not directly control unweighted monochromatic edges in reconstruction.

topics.title: Graph Isomorphism & Canonization
topics.summary: When do two differently labelled graphs encode exactly the same structure?
intro: Graph isomorphism asks whether one graph can be transformed into another merely by renaming its vertices. It belongs to NP, yet it has resisted both a polynomial-time algorithm and an NP-completeness proof. Practical programs solve many instances quickly, but the worst-case theory remains exceptional.

Babai’s breakthrough reduced the general worst-case running time to quasipolynomial. The surrounding theory combines permutation groups, combinatorics, logic, canonical labelling, and Weisfeiler–Leman refinement. It also connects to graph learning because useful representations should respect isomorphism without collapsing genuinely different graphs.

Graph reconstruction asks whether an unlabeled graph is determined by the complete multiset of its one-vertex-deleted subgraphs. Card isomorphisms need not align consistently. The new direction below records restricted attachment-recovery certificates and the remaining global alignment problem.

problems.title: Is general graph isomorphism solvable in polynomial time?
problems.lead: Babai gave a deterministic quasipolynomial-time algorithm, but no polynomial-time algorithm is known for unrestricted graphs.
problems.model: Input: two finite simple undirected graphs G,H on n vertices. They are isomorphic when a bijection φ preserves adjacency in both directions. The algorithm must work for every input, without degree or structural restrictions.
problems.statement: Does a deterministic algorithm decide whether G ≅ H in n^{O(1)} time?
problems.known: Babai proves a deterministic quasipolynomial-time algorithm. Neuen's 2026 survey still identifies unrestricted polynomial-time GI as open. Polynomial-time algorithms on restricted classes do not settle this question.
problems.formula: Known general upper bound: exp((log n)^{O(1)})  ·  Target: n^{O(1)}
problems.statusNote: The cited survey records the open status; no accepted general polynomial-time solution was located in the review. A research snapshot from 31 October 2026 is now recorded below; no unrestricted resolution is claimed.

research.currentGap: No deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for unrestricted graph isomorphism was established. Failure of selected invariants is not a lower bound against all algorithms.

results.title: Spectra plus ordinary color refinement are incomplete
results.claim: The rook and Shrikhande graphs have the same 16-vertex spectrum and color-refinement output, yet four-clique counts 8 and 0.
assumptions: Simple undirected unlabeled graphs.
The proposed invariant consists only of adjacency spectra and ordinary vertex color refinement.
results.argument: Both satisfy A² = 4I + 2J, giving spectrum 6^(1), 2^(6), (−2)^(9). The Shrikhande neighborhood is a 6-cycle, whereas the rook graph has row and column four-cliques.
results.limitation: This defeats that invariant combination only. Adding K4 counts distinguishes this pair but does not solve GI.

obstacles.route: Treat the spectrum and stable ordinary color refinement as a complete invariant.
obstacles.reason: The rook/Shrikhande pair is an exact counterexample.

problems.title: Is graph isomorphism fixed-parameter tractable in maximum degree?
problems.lead: Polynomial time for each fixed degree is known; a uniform exponent independent of the degree remains elusive.
problems.model: Both input graphs have n vertices and maximum degree at most d, with d≥2 (degrees 0 and 1 are elementary). Fixed-parameter tractability means time f(d) · n^C for a computable f and an absolute constant C independent of d.
problems.statement: Is there an isomorphism algorithm with running time f(d) · n^C for all n and d?
problems.known: Grohe, Neuen and Schweitzer obtain n^{O((log d)^c)} time for an absolute c. The exponent still depends on d; Neuen's 2026 survey, §4.1 after Corollary 4.7, explicitly records FPT in maximum degree as open.
problems.formula: Known: n^{O((log d)^c)}  ·  Target: f(d) · n^C
problems.statusNote: Explicit open-status statement in the survey; no later FPT resolution was located. A research snapshot from 31 October 2026 is now recorded below; no unrestricted resolution is claimed.
problems.importance: A uniform algorithmic guarantee for graphs of bounded degree

research.currentGap: An FPT algorithm in the number of branching vertices does not imply FPT in maximum degree: a cubic graph may have every vertex branching.

results.title: An FPT algorithm for a different parameter
results.claim: GI can be decided in t!·n^O(1) when t counts vertices of degree at least three.
assumptions: t is the count of branching vertices, not maximum degree d.
results.argument: Try all bijections of branch vertices. The remaining paths, cycles and isolated vertices are determined by their lengths and endpoint attachments to the branch set.
results.limitation: For cubic graphs t can equal n. This does not supply f(d)·n^C.

obstacles.route: Absorb the exponent a(d) in n^a(d) into a prefactor f(d).
obstacles.reason: For fixed d with a(d) > C, n^(a(d)−C) is unbounded as n increases.

obstacles.route: Use the branching-vertex algorithm with t bounded by d.
obstacles.reason: There is no such bound; arbitrary cubic graphs have t = n.

problems.title: Does the vertex-deleted deck determine every graph?
problems.lead: The Kelly-Ulam reconstruction conjecture remains open. A new notebook direction studies how to recover relative leaf attachments over a symmetric core.
problems.model: G is a finite simple undirected graph on n>=3 vertices. Its deck is the complete multiset of n unlabeled vertex-deleted induced subgraphs G-v. Repeated isomorphism types retain multiplicity; the vertex correspondence between cards is hidden.
problems.statement: Prove that graphs with identical full vertex-deleted decks are isomorphic, or give two nonisomorphic graphs on at least three vertices with rigorously identical full decks.
problems.known: McKay verified the full and set conjectures through 13 vertices and specified larger classes. Heinrich, Kiyomi, Otachi and Schweitzer prove interval graphs reconstructible in a 2026-revised paper. Contemporary 2026 primary papers continue to treat the general conjecture as open. Anchor and endvertex methods predate this notebook.
problems.source: Kelly-Ulam; 2026 primary literature; notebook draft 2 Nov 2026
problems.checked: Dufresne et al. 2026, Sections 1-3; Heinrich et al. v2, 12 May 2026; McKay v4, 2022
problems.statusNote: Full conjecture open in the primary sources checked on 2 November 2026. The notebook draft proves restricted sufficient criteria; novelty and independent validation are unassessed. Its finite checks do not extend the established 13-vertex benchmark.
problems.importance: Whether hidden global structure is uniquely determined by all of its one-vertex-deleted views

research.currentGap: The full Kelly-Ulam conjecture remains open. The new draft gives explicit certificates only for recognized leaf extensions of minimum-degree-two cores, with conditional path-signature separation or a multiplicity-gap condition. General cores and leaf-free graphs are not resolved. Independent proof review and comparison with established anchor/endvertex results are pending.

results.title: A draft certificate for two leaves over a symmetric core
results.claim: For G=H plus leaves a-x and b-y, n=h+2, the full deck recovers the unordered endpoint vertex-orbits and every simple-path count p_l^H(x,y), 0<=l<=h-2. If this signature identifies one unordered-pair orbit under Aut(H), G is reconstructible among all graphs with its deck.
assumptions: Finite simple undirected graphs; the full multiset of unlabeled one-vertex-deleted induced cards is given, including multiplicities.

The restricted model is a connected core H of order h with minimum degree at least two, plus leaves directly attached to core vertices. Recognition against arbitrary full-deck mates is part of the proof.
Path subgraph counts are ordinary, not induced; endpoint paths in H are vertex-simple. Only proper patterns with fewer than n vertices are recovered by Kelly counting.
The two attachment vertices may coincide. Signature separation is a stated hypothesis, not a universal theorem.
results.argument: Recover edge count and each deleted degree; leaf cards expose H and force any deck-mate to be the same type of leaf extension. Kelly counting gives c(P_k,G). Inclusion-exclusion c(P_k,G)-c(P_k,G-a)-c(P_k,G-b)+c(P_k,H) counts paths containing both leaves, which must be endpoints, hence equals p_(k-3)^H(x,y). A unique pair orbit then yields an isomorphism.
results.limitation: This extends the distance-only certificate in this notebook, not a claimed literature-first theorem. The anchor/endvertex framework is established. Separation has not been proved for arbitrary cores; automorphism and simple-path enumeration may be expensive. Independent review and novelty comparison are pending.

results.title: An explicit infinite family with nontrivial core symmetry
results.claim: Every graph obtained by attaching two leaves, allowing a shared base, to K_s box K_2 for s>=3 is reconstructed by the path certificate. The four pair signatures (p0,p1,p2) are (1,0,0), (0,1,s-2), (0,1,0), (0,0,2).
assumptions: Finite simple undirected graphs; the full multiset of unlabeled one-vertex-deleted induced cards is given, including multiplicities.

The restricted model is a connected core H of order h with minimum degree at least two, plus leaves directly attached to core vertices. Recognition against arbitrary full-deck mates is part of the proof.
Path subgraph counts are ordinary, not induced; endpoint paths in H are vertex-simple. Only proper patterns with fewer than n vertices are recovered by Kelly counting.
H consists of two s-cliques joined by a perfect matching; s>=3.
results.argument: Simultaneously permuting clique positions and swapping the two cliques acts transitively on each of the four listed pair types. Their path signatures differ, proving they are precisely the unordered-pair orbits. The general certificate applies using proper paths on at most five vertices.
results.limitation: A same-clique edge and a matching edge have equal distance and endpoint orbits; their common-neighbor counts differ. This is a self-contained sufficient-family proof, not a claim that the reconstructibility of this class was previously unknown.

results.title: Quadratic recovery of attachment multiplicities and a gap criterion
results.claim: For G=H(a) with r attached leaves, the leaf-card sum satisfies sum Q(b)=(r-2)Q(a)+r, Q(a)=sum a_v^2. If r!=2, any leaf card with exactly one coordinate of the inferred value (Q(a)-Q(b)-1)/2 restores a uniquely. In particular a positive occupancy with an absent predecessor suffices, and every r>h(h-1)/2 forces such a gap.
assumptions: Finite simple undirected graphs; the full multiset of unlabeled one-vertex-deleted induced cards is given, including multiplicities.

The restricted model is a connected core H of order h with minimum degree at least two, plus leaves directly attached to core vertices. Recognition against arbitrary full-deck mates is part of the proof.
Path subgraph counts are ordinary, not induced; endpoint paths in H are vertex-simple. Only proper patterns with fewer than n vertices are recovered by Kelly counting.
There may be any number r>=1 of directly attached leaves, with nonnegative integer multiplicities a_v. The moment formula can be inverted only for r!=2.
results.argument: Each card b=a-e_v occurs a_v times. Expanding the square gives the identity and the removed value q=(Q(a)-Q(b)+1)/2. A unique coordinate of value q-1 determines the completion. If no positive occupancy has an absent predecessor, all values 0..M occur; then r<=Mh-M(M+1)/2<=h(h-1)/2.
results.limitation: The strict threshold is sharp only for forcing this elementary gap; it is not a lower bound on reconstructibility. Lauri and the endvertex literature already provide strong group-action criteria. No priority or improvement over those results is claimed. The case r=2 needs other information.

results.title: A fixed path cutoff cannot handle every large core
results.claim: For every fixed L>=0, two nonisomorphic two-leaf extensions of C_(2L+5), at attachment distances L+1 and L+2, have the same leaf cards, endpoint vertex-orbits and p0..pL. On the triangular prism, four nonisomorphic two-leaf extensions even have the same entire leaf-deletion deck.
assumptions: Finite simple undirected graphs; the full multiset of unlabeled one-vertex-deleted induced cards is given, including multiplicities.

The restricted model is a connected core H of order h with minimum degree at least two, plus leaves directly attached to core vertices. Recognition against arbitrary full-deck mates is part of the proof.
Path subgraph counts are ordinary, not induced; endpoint paths in H are vertex-simple. Only proper patterns with fewer than n vertices are recovered by Kelly counting.
This compares restricted information: two leaf cards and a bounded path signature. It does not assert equality of the full vertex-deleted decks.
results.argument: The cycle is vertex-transitive. Both chosen pair distances exceed L, so all the listed simple-path counts vanish. The distances differ and are invariant under cycle automorphisms, making the full graphs nonisomorphic. For the prism, all single-leaf attachments lie in one orbit while unordered pairs have four orbits.
results.limitation: These are counterexamples to truncated or restricted reconstruction methods, not counterexamples to the Kelly-Ulam conjecture. The full proper profile separates the cycle pairs.

obstacles.route: Align two leaf cards independently and assume the joint attachment is fixed.
obstacles.reason: A vertex-transitive triangular-prism core has four unordered-pair orbits but all four two-leaf extensions have the same two leaf cards. Additional full-deck information is necessary.

obstacles.route: Use adjacency-matrix powers in place of the simple-path counts in the proof.
obstacles.reason: Matrix powers permit repeated vertices. The leaf endpoint bijection and Kelly occurrence counts use copies of an ordinary path graph with distinct vertices.

obstacles.route: Replace the full proper path profile by one fixed length cutoff for all graph sizes.
obstacles.reason: Cycle cores of order 2L+5 with attachment distances L+1 and L+2 defeat the cutoff L. This limits the method, not the full conjecture.

topics.title: Graphons, Sampling & Identifiability
topics.summary: How much of an infinite graph limit can finite random samples determine?
intro: Graphons W:[0,1]²→[0,1] describe dense graph limits, considered up to weak isomorphism rather than pointwise equality.
Cycle densities retain spectral information. Does equality of that information lift to finite cospectral approximations in cut distance?

problems.title: Can equal-density cospectral graphons resist finite cospectral approximation?
problems.lead: Cospectrality passes to graph limits; reversing that passage can fail. Is equal edge density enough to remove the obstruction?
problems.model: U,W are graphons with t(Ck,U)=t(Ck,W) for every k≥3 and ∫U=∫W. Here t is homomorphism density, Ck is a cycle, and δ□ is cut distance after measure-preserving relabeling. WG is the step graphon representing G.
problems.statement: Do such U,W exist for which no finite simple cospectral graph pairs Gj,Hj of equal order tending to infinity satisfy δ□(WGj,U)→0 and δ□(WHj,W)→0? Cospectral finite graphs have identical adjacency spectra, including multiplicities.
problems.known: The paper proves inapproximability when ∫U≠∫W. Equal edge density rules out that particular obstruction and is the remaining published question.
problems.formula: Equal cycle densities + equal edge density ⇒ finite cospectral approximation?
problems.statusNote: Explicitly open in the published paper; targeted later-work searches found no resolution. The preprint numbers it Problem 4.4. A research snapshot from 31 October 2026 is now recorded below; no unrestricted resolution is claimed.
problems.importance: Which spectral equivalences survive approximation by finite graphs?

backgroundResults.title: Finite graphs embed exactly into the graphon model
backgroundResults.explanation: A graphon is a symmetric measurable function W:[0,1]²→[0,1]. For a simple graph G on n vertices, divide [0,1] into n equal intervals and put its adjacency matrix on the resulting blocks. The binary graphon WG preserves normalized homomorphism counts, including maps that are not injective. Every graphon also admits a sequence of finite simple graphs converging to it in cut distance.
backgroundResults.relevance: Approximating each graphon separately is possible. The extra difficulty is keeping each approximating pair exactly cospectral.

backgroundResults.title: Cut convergence preserves every fixed simple-graph density
backgroundResults.explanation: Cut distance measures discrepancies on measurable rectangles after measure-preserving relabeling. The Counting Lemma bounds the change in t(F,W) for every fixed simple graph F. Consequently, if equal-order cospectral graph pairs converge to U and W, their equal cycle densities pass to the limits. This proves the forward implication behind the question.
backgroundResults.relevance: This continuity theorem supplies necessary conditions for approximation; it does not construct cospectral approximants.
backgroundResults.citation: Borgs et al. · Theorem 3.7(a), nonnegative-kernel refinement in §4.6.1

backgroundResults.title: Cycle densities determine the nonzero operator spectrum
backgroundResults.explanation: The operator (TWf)(x) = ∫W(x,y)f(y)dy is compact and self-adjoint on L². Its nonzero eigenvalues λᵢ are real and square-summable. The identities below express cycle densities as spectral moments. Knowing all moments for k ≥ 3 recovers these eigenvalues, including multiplicities.
backgroundResults.relevance: Spectra fix ∫W², generally not ∫W. Cycle moments cannot detect the zero eigenspace's dimension.

backgroundResults.title: Cospectral graphons can have different edge densities
backgroundResults.explanation: For U ≡ 1/2 and W = 1[0,1/2]² (the indicator of the half-square), both operators have rank one with sole nonzero eigenvalue 1/2. Their edge densities differ.
backgroundResults.relevance: Equal edge density is an extra assumption, not implied by cospectrality.
backgroundResults.citation: On cospectral graphons · preprint Theorem 4.2 / journal Theorem 5

backgroundResults.title: Exact finite cospectrality forces equal edge counts
backgroundResults.explanation: Each edge gives two closed walks of length two, so tr(AG²) = 2|E(G)|. Equal adjacency spectra therefore force equal edges and, at common order n, equal normalized densities. Edge-density continuity passes this equality to graphon limits.
backgroundResults.relevance: This explains why the question requires equal edge density.

backgroundResults.title: Unequal density gives a quantitative obstruction
backgroundResults.explanation: Binary cospectral approximants U′,W′ have equal spectral square sums. Since V² = V for binary V, their edge densities agree. Edge-density continuity and the triangle inequality give this derived obstruction. For the example above, the total cut error is at least 1/4.
backgroundResults.relevance: Equal density makes this lower bound zero, so a new obstruction is needed.
backgroundResults.citation: Derived from preprint Proposition 4.3 / journal Proposition 6

backgroundResults.title: A related equivalence does admit simultaneous approximation
backgroundResults.explanation: Fractional isomorphism of graphons is characterized by equality of all finite-tree densities. Hladký and Hng prove that any family of fractionally isomorphic graphons can be approximated, within any prescribed cut error, by jointly fractionally isomorphic finite graphs of every sufficiently large common order. Their theorem is an established positive result for preserving an equivalence during finite approximation.
backgroundResults.relevance: The result concerns tree densities. It gives useful precedent, but does not guarantee adjacency-cospectral approximants for the present cycle-density question.

problems.backgroundConclusion: Whether a cospectral pair with equal edge density can still resist finite cospectral approximation remains open. Neither the unequal-density counterexample nor the fractional-isomorphism approximation theorem settles that case.

research.currentGap: A resistant equal-density pair is not known here. Approximation of limiting moments is insufficient: every finite pair must have exactly the same characteristic polynomial.

results.title: A whole rank-two family is approximable
results.claim: All cospectral complete bipartite graphons with isolates admit simultaneous finite cospectral approximation.
assumptions: B_(a,b) has complete edges between disjoint sets of masses a,b and zero elsewhere.
a+b ≤ 1, c+d ≤ 1, and ab = cd.
results.argument: Approximate a,b,c rationally and set d′ = a′b′/c′; after a common shrink the support constraints have slack. A common denominator gives equal-order K_(Na′,Nb′) and K_(Nc′,Nd′) with equal spectra.
results.limitation: This treats only complete bipartite graphons with isolates, not arbitrary cospectral graphons.

obstacles.route: Reuse the unequal-edge-density obstruction in the equal-density question.
obstacles.reason: The required density equality makes that lower bound zero.

obstacles.route: Independently sample both limits and infer exact finite cospectrality.
obstacles.reason: Agreement of asymptotic moments does not give identical finite characteristic polynomials.

topics.title: Regularity, Removal & Quantitative Bounds
topics.summary: Can qualitative decomposition theorems become efficient enough to power real algorithms?
intro: Regularity lemmas approximate a large graph by a bounded collection of pseudorandom pieces. They drive results in graph limits, property testing, counting, and removal, but their worst-case partition sizes can grow as towers of exponentials.

This creates a sharp divide between qualitative existence and useful quantitative bounds. Research asks which graph classes admit polynomial or singly exponential decompositions and whether weaker regularity retains enough information for testing and estimation.

problems.title: Narrow the quantitative gap in triangle removal
problems.lead: A polynomial removal bound is already ruled out. The remaining gap runs from quasipolynomial growth to a tower.
problems.model: Let T(G) count unordered triangles and τ△(G) be the fewest edge deletions making G triangle-free. Define δ△(ε)=inf T(G)/n³ over all positive integers n and all eligible n-vertex graphs with τ△(G)≥εn². tower(h) denotes a tower of twos of height h.
problems.statement: Determine sharper asymptotic upper or lower bounds for δ△(ε) as ε→0, reducing the gap between the known construction and removal guarantees.
problems.known: Fox's removal argument gives a tower of height O(log(1/ε)) for 1/δ△. Behrend-type constructions give exp(Ω(log²(1/ε))); Hunter's 2025 construction improves the constant while retaining this form.
problems.statusNote: The 2026 paper explicitly calls narrowing this gap open; no subsequent resolution was located. A research snapshot from 31 October 2026 is now recorded below; no unrestricted resolution is claimed.
problems.importance: Quantitative foundations of removal and dense graph testing

research.currentGap: No new unrestricted bound narrows the quasipolynomial-to-tower gap. The tripartite calculation and progression-free construction are restricted or standard arguments.

results.title: Exact complete-tripartite behavior
results.claim: For a complete tripartite core plus isolates, τ/n² = min(ab,ac,bc) and T/n³ = abc; ε-farness implies T ≥ ε^(3/2)n³.
assumptions: One complete tripartite core, with all other vertices isolated.
results.argument: A Latin-rectangle triangle packing supplies min(AB,AC,BC) edge-disjoint triangles. Multiplying ab,ac,bc yields (abc)² ≥ ε³.
results.limitation: This does not improve general triangle removal; the exponent is sharp only within the stated class.

obstacles.route: Use edge-disjoint triangle packing alone to derive a uniform cubic-scale count.
obstacles.reason: Packing may supply order εn² triangles, whereas removal needs a bound on the n³ scale; progression-free examples expose this gap.

nextTasks.question: Specify a genuine extension of the tripartite-core class and quantify how overlap among triangles is controlled.
nextTasks.acceptance: Prove a cubic-scale triangle lower bound from ε-farness under explicit extra hypotheses, and show with examples why those hypotheses matter.

nextTasks.acceptance: Give an exact proof or a finite counterexample, distinguishing the standard construction from Hunter’s stronger constants.

problems.title: Does induced C₄ removal admit a polynomial bound?
problems.lead: The induced four-cycle case has an exponential guarantee, while a polynomial guarantee remains conjectural.
problems.model: An induced C₄ is a set of four vertices spanning a cycle with no diagonal edges. Distance to induced-C₄-freeness allows both edge additions and deletions, normalized by n².
problems.statement: Do absolute constants a,b>0 exist such that every n-vertex graph requiring at least εn² edge edits to become induced-C₄-free contains at least aε^b n⁴ induced copies of C₄?
problems.known: Gishboliner and Shapira prove a lower bound 2^{−(1/ε)^C} n⁴ for some absolute C>0. Gishboliner's 2025 notes restate the polynomial improvement as Conjecture 3.6. Labeled versus unlabeled copies changes only the constant factor.
problems.formula: Known: 2^{−poly(1/ε)} n⁴ copies  ·  Conjectured: poly(ε) n⁴ copies
problems.statusNote: Explicit conjecture in the author's notes; 2025–2026 searches found no polynomial removal theorem settling it. A research snapshot from 31 October 2026 is now recorded below; no unrestricted resolution is claimed.

research.currentGap: The polynomial guarantee was proved only for triangle-free inputs. In general, ordinary four-cycles need not be induced, and edge deletion can create induced copies.

results.title: A polynomial induced-C4 bound for triangle-free inputs
results.claim: Every triangle-free n-vertex graph ε-far under arbitrary edits from induced-C4-freeness has at least (ε^5/4)n^4 induced copies.
assumptions: The input is triangle-free.
0 < ε ≤ 1; edits may be additions or deletions.
Copies are unordered four-vertex sets.
results.argument: Distance gives m ≥ εn² and Q ≥ εn². Common-neighbor counting yields Q ≥ ε⁴n⁴/4 for n ≥ ε^(−2); the first bound handles smaller n.
results.limitation: Triangle-freeness is essential to the argument; this does not prove the unrestricted polynomial conjecture.

obstacles.route: Apply ordinary C4 supersaturation to unrestricted input graphs.
obstacles.reason: Complete graphs have many ordinary four-cycles but no induced C4. Deletions can also create induced copies.

nextTasks.title: Extend the bound to inputs with few triangles
nextTasks.question: Find an explicit robustness theorem when the graph has a quantified triangle density or can be made triangle-free cheaply.
nextTasks.acceptance: Account for induced C4 copies created or destroyed by all edits; provide a polynomial bound with every extra hypothesis explicit.

nextTasks.title: Audit the all-orders ε^5/4 proof
nextTasks.question: Check the n < ε^(−2) case and that edit distance permits additions as well as deletions.
nextTasks.acceptance: Produce an independent written proof or a finite counterexample; finite tests alone do not certify the asymptotic claim.

topics.title: Learning on Graphs
topics.summary: When can graph neural networks generalize across size, density, and topology?
intro: Graph neural networks process data whose relationships matter as much as individual features. Their expressive power is tied to graph isomorphism tests, while their stability and transfer across graphs can be studied through graph limits and graphon operators.

The question below concerns a fixed network applied to graphs sampled from the same graphon. Quantitative bounds must specify the architecture, activation, and signal assumptions. Size transfer alone does not establish generalization after training or transfer between different graph distributions.

problems.title: Quantitative transferability of higher-order graphon networks
problems.lead: A draft now gives explicit arbitrary fixed-depth Lipschitz rates and sharp regularity examples. Independent review and novelty assessment remain open.
problems.model: Fix an Invariant Graphon Network N (IWN) with architecture and weights independent of n,m and continuous activation. W:[0,1]²→[0,1] is symmetric measurable; f is scalar measurable, ||f||∞≤r>1. Independently sample simple loopless graph-signals using iid uniform positions, conditional Bernoulli(W(xi,xj)) edges, and f(xi) signals.
problems.statement: Obtain explicit, tight bounds on E|N(Gn,fn)−N(Gm,fm)| beyond the restricted two-layer analytic architecture. Track tensor order, depth, weights, signal bound, and activation regularity.
problems.known: Published Theorem 5.2/Corollary 5.3 give qualitative transferability; Theorem 5.4 treats a restricted analytic two-layer class. A 2 November 2026 notebook draft derives a direct root-n sampling rate at arbitrary fixed Lipschitz depth for the normalized partial-matching basis, together with sharp Hölder powers. The draft is not independently reviewed.
problems.formula: Draft, n,m>=2K: E|N_n-N_m| <= P_L[(n-K)^(-1/2)+(m-K)^(-1/2)] + Q_L(1/n+1/m). Explicit layer constants and exact scope are in the proof.
problems.checked: Primary literature checked 2 Nov 2026; draft proof awaits independent review; novelty unassessed
problems.statusNote: Full problem remains open. The new draft addresses bounded same-source sampling for fixed normalized partial-matching IWNs. It is not a distribution-shift or trained-model guarantee, and its independent verification and publication novelty remain unassessed.
problems.importance: Finite-sample guarantees for expressive graph models

research.currentGap: A 2 November 2026 draft now gives architecture-level root-n rates at arbitrary fixed Lipschitz depth in the normalized partial-matching IWN class, explicit modulus/Hölder rates, and a sharp nonlinear three-layer example. The conditional induction, exact architectural coverage and literature novelty still need independent audit. Full partition-basis operations, optimal architecture-specific constants and broader sampling models are outside the claim. No unrestricted resolution has been accepted.

results.title: A direct root-n sampling bound for local networks
results.claim: For a bounded ordered-k local kernel |h| ≤ M, E|N_n−N_m| ≤ Mk(n^(−1/2)+m^(−1/2)) + Mk(k−1)(n^(−1)+m^(−1)).
assumptions: Fixed k and n,m ≥ k; normalized averages over all ordered tuples.
Independent simple loopless graph-signals sampled from one fixed graphon-signal.
The kernel depends only on the tuple’s internal edges and signals.
results.argument: Injective tuple kernels on disjoint vertex sets are independent, so their average has variance at most M²k²/n. Noninjective tuples change the average by at most Mk(k−1)/n.
results.limitation: The limit integrates Bernoulli edge randomness; it need not equal the same formula evaluated directly on W. The result does not cover a nonlinear activation after global pooling.

results.title: An explicit coefficient-dependent bound at fixed polynomial depth
results.claim: A finite motif expansion has transfer bound A(n^(−1/2)+m^(−1/2)) + B(n^(−1)+m^(−1)), with A = Σ|c_j|r^D_j v_j and B = Σ|c_j|r^D_j v_j(v_j−1).
assumptions: A finite loopless multigraph motif expansion is supplied.
Signals are bounded by r; model parameters are independent of sample size.
results.argument: Apply the local-kernel bound to each motif. Collapse parallel edges in the Bernoulli sampling limit.
results.limitation: This may have very large expansion constants. It is not a tight depth/width/order theorem.

results.title: No common rate shape for all continuous activations
results.claim: For any proposed positive rate tending to zero, some single fixed continuous activation and fixed network violate an O(r_n+r_m) transfer bound.
assumptions: The network may apply a continuous activation to a globally averaged Rademacher signal.
Activation regularity is unrestricted beyond continuity.
results.argument: Prescribe a continuous increasing modulus on a sequence of typical sample-mean scales. A fourth-moment Paley–Zygmund bound supplies a uniform fluctuation probability, forcing a slower sequence.
results.limitation: This does not rule out root-n behavior for normalized Lipschitz architectures or activation-modulus-dependent rates.

results.title: A draft root-n bound at arbitrary fixed Lipschitz depth
results.claim: For the normalized partial-matching IWN class, E|N_n-mu| <= P_L/sqrt(n-K)+Q_L/n. Hence E|N_n-N_m| <= P_L[(n-K)^(-1/2)+(m-K)^(-1/2)]+Q_L(1/n+1/m), uniformly over bounded graphon-signals. P_0=Q_0=0; P_l=L_l a_l(P_(l-1)+M_(l-1) r_l), Q_l=L_l a_l(Q_(l-1)+2M_(l-1)d_l), d_l=k_l r_l+r_l(r_l-1)/2.
assumptions: Fixed finite depth, tensor orders, channel widths and weights, independently of sample size; scalar output, K=max tensor order and n,m>=2K.

Simple loopless symmetric Bernoulli graph samples from one arbitrary measurable graphon W; iid uniform latent positions and one independent edge uniform per unordered pair; bounded measurable signal |f|<=R.

Every linear map is a finite linear combination of normalized partial matchings: r free input indices are summed over all tuples with factor n^(-r), including repetitions. No within-input diagonal extraction or output equality masks.
Constant channel biases and pointwise activations with the specified Lipschitz or continuity modulus on bounded reachable intervals. The last activation may be the identity.
The deterministic limit integrates conditional Bernoulli tuple types; it need not equal the original weighted-input network N(W,f).
L_l is the layer activation Lipschitz constant; a_l is the maximum absolute weight row sum; r_l is the maximum free input order among nonzero weights; M_l bounds finite tensors and limiting fields.
results.argument: Construct a bounded conditional tuple field at each layer. First replace the globally dependent hidden tensor by that local field in unconditional mean. Conditional on the entire output tuple type, kernels on disjoint fresh vertex sets are independent. Their averaging error is at most M r/sqrt(n-q), and collisions cost at most 2M[qr+r(r-1)/2]/n. Lipschitz induction gives the constants. An L1 contraction argument also yields a stated bounded-differences concentration corollary.
results.limitation: This is a self-contained draft, not an independently checked or novelty-certified theorem. It excludes full diagonal partition-basis operations, sparse/unbounded sampling, sample-size-dependent parameters and distribution shift. Constants may be loose or grow rapidly with depth; it is not a runtime or learning guarantee.

results.title: Explicit continuous-modulus recursion and sharp Hölder powers
results.claim: For continuous activations, e_l(n) <= Omega_l(a_l[e_(l-1)(n)+eta_l(n)]), with eta_l=M_(l-1)[r_l/sqrt(n-K)+2d_l/n] and an explicit concave majorant Omega_l of the activation modulus. If layer l is alpha_l-Hölder, the rate is O(n^(-beta)+m^(-beta)), beta=(1/2) product_l alpha_l. This exponent is worst-case sharp within the stated class.
assumptions: Fixed finite depth, tensor orders, channel widths and weights, independently of sample size; scalar output, K=max tensor order and n,m>=2K.

Simple loopless symmetric Bernoulli graph samples from one arbitrary measurable graphon W; iid uniform latent positions and one independent edge uniform per unordered pair; bounded measurable signal |f|<=R.

Every linear map is a finite linear combination of normalized partial matchings: r free input indices are summed over all tuples with factor n^(-r), including repetitions. No within-input diagonal extraction or output equality masks.
Constant channel biases and pointwise activations with the specified Lipschitz or continuity modulus on bounded reachable intervals. The last activation may be the identity.
The deterministic limit integrates conditional Bernoulli tuple types; it need not equal the original weighted-input network N(W,f).

For the Hölder conclusion, 0<alpha_l<=1 and a finite Hölder constant is specified for each activation on its reachable preactivation interval. Sharpness is over the class of architectures, not for every architecture.
results.argument: Use Omega(t)=inf_(delta>0)(1+t/delta)omega(delta), Omega(0)=0; segment subdivision shows omega<=Omega<=2omega and the infimum is concave. Apply Jensen to the conditional-averaging bound. Hölder Jensen multiplies the exponent at each layer. For sharpness, integrate an iid Rademacher signal and successively apply |t|^(alpha_l): the output is |sample mean|^(product alpha_l); a central limit argument with uniform integrability gives a positive matching constant for independent equal-size transfer.
results.limitation: The modulus-dependent recursion does not give a common rate for arbitrary continuous activations. Worst-case power sharpness does not establish optimal architecture-specific constants. Independent proof and novelty review are pending.

results.title: A nonlinear three-layer example with a matching root-n obstruction
results.claim: For H1(i,j,k)=ReLU(A_ik+A_jk-1), H2(i,j)=ReLU(n^(-1)sum_k H1-theta), N_n=n^(-2)sum_(i,j)H2, theta in [0,1], E|N_n-mu_theta| <= (3/2-theta)/sqrt(n)+(3-theta)/n. For W identically p and theta=p^2, sqrt(n) E N_n -> sqrt[p^2(1-p^2)/(2 pi)]>0. Sizes n and n^2 therefore have a matching root-n transfer obstruction.
assumptions: Orders 2->3->2->0; three affine layers, two ReLUs and an identity readout; all ordered tuples included; A_ii=0.
Independent simple Bernoulli graph samples from one W; fixed theta in [0,1]. For sharpness choose 0<p<1, constant W=p, and theta=p^2.
mu_theta = integral_(x,y) (integral_z W(x,z)W(y,z) dz-theta)_+ dxdy.
results.argument: Condition on an off-diagonal pair: its common-neighbor sum is Bin(n-2,q), giving a 1/(2sqrt(n))+2/n approximation. The remaining bounded latent-pair U-statistic contributes (1-theta)/sqrt(n), with a (1-theta)/n diagonal correction. For constant W the exact expectation is a sum of two binomial positive-part expectations; the binomial central limit theorem gives the positive root-n constant.
results.limitation: Finite exhaustive checks corroborate the explicit binomial identity, not the asymptotic proof. The lower bound uses unequal sizes n and n^2; the separate Rademacher example establishes equal-size sharpness across the general class. Independent review and novelty assessment remain pending.

obstacles.route: Identify the finite-sample limit with N(W,f) for every nonlinear network.
obstacles.reason: For example, averaging A_ij² tends to ∫W, whereas evaluating the square formula on W gives ∫W².

obstacles.route: Claim one algebraic or logarithmic rate for all continuous activations.
obstacles.reason: A single fixed activation can be constructed with arbitrarily slow fluctuations after global pooling.

obstacles.route: Treat distinct hidden-tensor summands as conditionally independent before replacing them by local type fields.
obstacles.reason: The actual hidden tensor depends on the whole sampled graph. The draft first compares it to a local field in unconditional mean; only the local field is eligible for the fresh-set covariance argument.
